decisions.reason: The solenoid decision does not alter the existing leak-prevention requirements; the source merely reiterates sealing and no-leak behavior already present.
Changing the dispensing valve to a solenoid does not invalidate or modify the existing requirement that the spout be removable or cleanable.
The internal valve mechanism and dispensing sequence do not change the spout's location, orientation, appearance, construction, or beverage-quality constraint.
The controlled-dispensing modification does not change the required mixing result; the same message's separate strong-and-frothy texture statement is already represented under this candidate.
The solenoid dispensing decision does not change the independently stated mixing splash target, which already has a same-message MODIFY covering the splash guard policy.
The dispensing mechanism change does not alter quick bowl removal or swapping; the source message's separate bowl-cleaning clause is already represented by a same-message candidate Event.
The candidate already permits custom fabrication of the render-style dispensing spout, so retaining the solenoid approach creates no further change to its current sourcing policy.
The valve mechanism, dispensing sequence, and flow behavior do not change bowl capacity or form.
The controlled-dispensing modification has no effect on machine wording, display name, or placard placement.
The solenoid and flow-control decision does not affect the established beige and green color scheme.
The source selects a product mechanism but does not change the obligation to provide component selection and a BOM or its stated deliverable scope.
The dispensing modification does not change the whisk configuration; the source's separate question about alternative whisk materials does not establish a replacement choice.
